proposal.description: The clean-run streak is broken only on a switching-cycle boundary, so leaving S_RUN or a window trip between PWM falls leaves the saturated clean count standing
proposal.reason: After a long clean run (clean_counter at clean_run_target), a window_trip moves the supervisor to S_HICCUP, which has no switching-cycle boundary. The count survives the hiccup entry, so on the next clock strike_level drops back to 0 and the strike that hiccup earned is wiped. Repeated faults then never escalate the cool-down or reach latch_assert.

proposal.description: Leaving S_RUN only pauses the clean-run count instead of clearing it; only window_trip restarts the streak
proposal.reason: Take a run that reaches clean_run_target and then leaves S_RUN through S_OFF (g_en low). The count stays at the target through S_OFF and S_SS. If a window_trip_SS hiccup follows, strike_level is cleared on the clock after its entry, so soft-start strikes never add up to latch_assert.

proposal.description: The latch is armed on the run-window trip that leads to the final hiccup, one clock before that hiccup is entered
proposal.reason: When strike_level is already max_strikes-1 and window_trip fires in S_RUN, latch_assert rises on that clock instead of one clock later on the S_HICCUP entry. The supervisor and the fault log therefore see the latch a cycle early.

proposal.description: The strike count saturates at MAX_STRIKES, so after the host lowers MAX_STRIKES below the count already reached, the latching hiccup is not counted
proposal.reason: Example: strike_level is 2 and the host writes MAX_STRIKES=1. The next hiccup still trips latch_assert, but strike_level stays at 2 instead of going to 3, so the strike_level reported for telemetry is one short.

proposal.description: A guard against the max_strikes-1 underflow is written with the wrong limit, so MAX_STRIKES=1 disables the latch
proposal.reason: With MAX_STRIKES written to 1 (the minimum reg_file allows), the first hiccup should assert latch_assert. Under this fault latch_assert never asserts, and strike_level keeps counting and wrapping on every later hiccup.
